A friend convinced me to try a pottery class with her.
She described it as relaxing and meditative.
Honestly, that sounded exactly like something I needed after a stressful few weeks at work.
We showed up, got our aprons, and sat down at these spinning wheels.
We watched the instructor make it look absurdly easy.
She shaped a perfect little bowl in what felt like about thirty seconds.
I pressed my hands into the clay the way she showed us.
For about ten seconds, it actually looked like something, a small, wobbly, but recognizable shape starting to form under my fingers.
I remember thinking, honestly, that maybe I had some hidden natural talent for this.
I even glanced around the room to see if anyone was noticing my apparently effortless progress on the wheel.
Nobody was watching, obviously, since everyone else was busy with their own clay.
But for that brief ten seconds, I genuinely felt like I had this whole pottery thing figured out.
Then I got a little too confident.
I pressed slightly too hard on one side, and my careful little bowl instantly collapsed.
It looked more like a deflated pancake than any kind of dinnerware.
I tried to fix it.
I added more clay and pressed here and there, but that just made things worse.
Within another minute I had what can only be described as a small clay volcano, lopsided and strange.
At one point I pressed the pedal a little too hard too, and the whole wheel spun so fast that a chunk of wet clay actually flew off.
It landed somewhere near my friend's feet, and she found that significantly funnier than I did.
My friend, meanwhile, was next to me calmly shaping an actual, recognizable mug.
She kept glancing over with an expression somewhere between sympathy and barely contained laughter at my little disaster.
The instructor came by and looked at my creation for a moment.
She said, kindly, that some pieces are "more about the process than the outcome." I'm pretty sure that's instructor code for "this is not going to be a mug."
I ended up keeping it anyway, glazed in a slightly too-bright blue.
It now sits on my kitchen counter holding loose change and random keys, doing a job that's honestly more useful than being an actual bowl.
I haven't gone back to pottery since.
But I still tell people I made that little dish myself, leaving out the part where it was originally supposed to be something completely different.
My friend still uses her actual mug every morning, and every time I see a picture of it, I feel a small, entirely reasonable amount of jealousy.
